Profound’s rapid growth and record funding signal a shift where AI-driven search visibility is now recognised as essential infrastructure, reshaping the marketing landscape with major enterprise clients and multi-billion dollar valuations\.

What once looked like a niche marketing tactic is now being priced as serious infrastructure\. A wave of venture money has turned AI search visibility into a recognisable category, with Profound at the centre of the trade\. In February 2026, the New York company raised $96 million in a Series C led by Lightspeed Venture Partners at a $1 billion valuation, lifting total funding to more than $155 million and giving the market a clear signal that helping brands surface in AI-generated answers is no longer an experimental side bet\. According to company statements and deal coverage, Profound now serves more than 700 enterprises, including major names such as Target, Figma, Walmart, Ramp, MongoDB, Chime and US Bank\.

The size and speed of the round matter as much as the valuation\. Profound was founded less than two years ago, yet it has already attracted repeat backing from Sequoia Capital and Kleiner Perkins, alongside Lightspeed in the latest round\. That combination suggests investors are treating the company less as a conventional martech vendor and more as a piece of core AI-era marketing infrastructure\. The company says its software is designed to help brands understand, influence and scale how they appear across AI search engines, a problem that has become more urgent as consumers increasingly start product research inside chatbots rather than in traditional search\.

That spread matters because it suggests the market is not being built around a single winner\. Instead, venture firms are taking positions across measurement, optimisation, discovery and, eventually, the agency and enterprise layers that sit above them\.

The clearest lesson from the cap table is that AI visibility is being assessed as a platform shift, not a feature add-on\. Profound’s latest funding round sets the benchmark, but it also helps explain why similar tools are drawing capital in both the US and Europe\. If AI systems become a primary route through which consumers discover brands, then the companies that can shape how those systems describe products and services may become as strategically important as search agencies were in the Google era\.

Profound, a New York-based startup developing marketing technologies, announced a Series C fundinground of $96 million, making it a $1 billion company, earning it a spot as an AI era unicorn\.

Led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, followed by Sequoia Capital, Kleiner Perkins, Saga VC, South Park Commons, and Evantic Capital\. With funding, Profound has increased total funding received to more than $155 million since its founding 18 months ago\.

Profound was founded to support enterprise brands in monitoring, analyzing, and improving recommendations of products and services in AI-generated responses\. The way users search has shifted from keyword searches to conversational AI models and answer engines\. The heart of Profound’s platform is an advanced analytics engine that interrogates AI models and retrieves structured outputs\.

## Profound Agents: From Insight to Execution

A major innovation from the latest round of funding that has created a lot of buzz is Profound Agents – fully autonomous AI workers that are customizable and provide an execution bridge for insights\. Traditionally, marketing teams had to export monitoring data and run campaigns on different systems\.

With Profound Agents built into the core platform, users can automate content creation, campaign workflows, and other processes\. These agents can draft optimized content, alter messages, and autonomously launch campaigns in the voice of the marketer\. There is rich value created for marketing enterprise teams, as the time between strategy and real results is reduced\. There is a positive impact on the output and efficiency\.

This proposition has been largely appreciated by big enterprises\. Profound now has over 700 clients globally and over 10% of the Fortune 500, including Target, Walmart, MongoDB, Figma, Ramp, Chime, and U\.S\. Bank, that are pioneering and amplifying the adoption of AI-led marketing techniques\.

## Competitive Landscape and Company Vision

Profound presently has fewer than 120 employees\. Yet it competes in a tough environment where many companies fight for top talent in AI and venture capital\. CEO James Cadwallader and his co-founder have said their vision for the company includes more than just tracking visibility; they envision Profound as the foundational technology for AI-assisted brand discovery, relaying the information to consumers\. Investors support this vision\.

Sachin Patel of Lightspeed Venture Partners stated that Profound’s technology is groundbreaking in terms of how marketing will be done in what he describes as an agentic world; a world where autonomous technologies and AI answer engines initiate the consumer-brand interactions\.

This recent round of funding will enable Profound to increase the pace of developing its technology and marketing it to more enterprise customers, as well as enhancing its autonomous agents, thereby establishing the company as a front-runner in the new area of Answer Engine Optimization \(AEO\) — the next area of focus after search engine optimization\.

Profound, an 18-month-old startup betting that the future of marketing will be shaped not by Google links but by AI answers, is now a unicorn\.

The company has raised its $96 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation\. Lightspeed Venture Partners led the round, with continued participation by Sequoia Capital, Kleiner Perkins, Evantic Capital, Saga VC, and South Park Commons, *Fortune* has learned\. The round brings total funding to $155 million and follows its Series B, which *Fortune* previously reported as one of the more aggressive early bets on “answer‑engine optimization” in the generative AI era\.

For decades, marketers have fought to climb search rankings\. Those days are fading fast, Profound CEO and cofounder James Cadwallader told *Fortune*\. Profound, he says, is reshaping how we experience “search”by helping brands measure, and ultimately influence, what systems like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity say about them\.

“In the future, every company on the planet will care deeply about how AI talks about and surfaces—and at some point interacts with—their brand,” Cadwallader said\. “As long as marketing exists, Profound has a place\.”

Profound’s software tracks how AI models describe and recommend brands across millions of real prompts\. It can show customers not just whether they appear in AI answers, but why and what competitors are doing differently\.

That level of insight is becoming increasingly critical as AI assistants displace traditional search: Instead of scanning pages of results, users now receive a single synthesized answer\.

“There’s this massive migration happening, where consumer attention is moving from search engines into answer engines,” Lightspeed partner Sachin Patel told *Fortune*\. “Profound is building the system of record for marketers in that world—the place where they understand and shape how AI represents their brand\.”

Profound already works with more than 700 enterprise customers and 10% of the Fortune 500 companies, including Target, Walmart, Ramp, MongoDB, U\.S\. Bank, and Figma\. The company says customers have used its platform to increase AI visibility in weeks, in some cases dramatically improving how often their brands appear in AI-generated recommendations\.

This reflects how fluid AI-driven discovery remains\. Profound’s internal research found that up to 90% of cited sources in AI answers can change over time, and that different models rely on largely distinct sets of sources\. In practice, that means brands must actively manage their presence across multiple AI ecosystems, rather than optimizing once for a single search engine\.

Cadwallader sees this shift as an expansion of SEO, not its extinction\.

“There’s this idea that SEO is dead, and I very much disagree,” he said\. “Our business is built on the shoulders of SEO, but this is way bigger\.”

That evolution is also reshaping marketing roles\. Traditional SEO specialists are becoming what Cadwallader calls “marketing engineers”—operators who combine analytics, automation, and AI systems to influence how models interpret and recommend products\.

Profound is investing heavily to stay ahead\. The company has fewer than 120 employees but is competing for talent with top AI labs and well-funded startups, and Cadwallader is out hiring\.\. Profound has also just launched Profound Agents, which helps generate and distribute marketing copy in a company’s voice\.

# Ex-Swiggy, Zomato leaders launch AI hiring platform Profound, raise $1\.5 million seed funding

Former technology executives from Swiggy, Zomato, Flipkart, Ola, Cleartrip and Walmart Labs have launched Profound, an artificial intelligence-powered platform designed to reshape professional networking and hiring through personalised AI representatives\. The startup has also secured $1\.5 million in seed funding as it prepares to expand its early-access programme\.

Founded by Anuj Rathi and Prashant Parashar, Profound is positioning itself as an AI-native alternative to traditional professional profiles and resumes\. Instead of relying on static information such as job titles or listed skills, the platform creates an AI representative for every user after an in-depth voice conversation, allowing it to build a richer understanding of an individual's experience, decision-making style, expertise and career aspirations\.

The funding round drew participation from several prominent technology entrepreneurs, including Swiggy CEO Sriharsha Majety, Swiggy co-founder Nandan Reddy, former Zomato executive Pankaj Chaddah, Razorpay CEO Harshil Mathur, WhatsApp Global Head Kunal Shah and OfBusiness co-founder Bhuvan Gupta\. Venture capital firms Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital also participated in the round\.

**AI representatives for professionals and employers**

Profound's platform is designed to support both job seekers and recruiters\.

For professionals, the AI representative continuously identifies relevant career opportunities, recommends valuable connections and facilitates introductions that could lead to new roles or collaborations\.

On the employer side, hiring managers can also create AI representatives for open positions\. Instead of filling out conventional job descriptions, recruiters describe roles through natural conversations, enabling the platform to capture details such as team culture, expectations, work style and organisational context\.

The company says its AI-powered matching engine then evaluates compatibility between candidates and employers using this broader contextual understanding rather than relying primarily on keyword-based searches\.

**Building an AI-first professional network**

Profound's long-term vision extends beyond recruitment\. The founders envision an ecosystem where AI representatives interact with one another on behalf of professionals, employers and organisations, enabling more relevant introductions and improving how talent is discovered\.

According to CEO Anuj Rathi, the platform aims to make professional representation accessible to everyone by providing users with an AI assistant that continuously understands their work, achievements and career goals\.

CTO Prashant Parashar said recent advances in voice AI have made it possible to capture deeper professional context through natural conversations, allowing AI systems to evaluate candidates beyond what traditional resumes or online profiles reveal\.

**Expansion plans**

Profound is currently onboarding users through an invite-only early-access programme, with a broader beta launch planned later this year\.

The startup plans to onboard one million professionals globally over the next 12 months while expanding its engineering, product development and artificial intelligence teams\.

Investors backing the company believe recruitment is increasingly shifting away from static profiles toward AI-driven evaluation models that can better assess judgement, work style and role compatibility, positioning startups like Profound to benefit as enterprises adopt AI-led hiring workflows\.

# Ex-Swiggy, Zomato execs raises $1\.5 mn for AI career startup

Profound founders Anuj Rathi and Prashant Parashar

Bengaluru: Former Swiggy executive Anuj Rathi and former Zomato chief technology officer Prashant Parashar have raised $1\.5 million in seed funding for Profound, an AI startup building digital representatives for professionals\.The round saw participation from Swiggy co-founders Sriharsha Majety and Nandan Reddy, former Zomato co-founder Pankaj Chaddah, Razorpay co-founder Harshil Mathur, Cred founder Kunal Shah and OfBusiness co-founder Bhuvan Gupta\. Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital also invested\.Profound creates an “AI Rep” through a voice conversation lasting about 30 minutes\. The system seeks to understand a person’s career, expertise, goals, preferences and working style\. It can then help prepare professional profiles and introductions, and match users with jobs and other connections\.“The way I think about Profound is that we want to create a global AI platform that gives every professional their own AI Rep,” Rathi told TOI\. “Athletes have agents and actors have managers\. Professionals should have an AI representative that understands them deeply\.”The startup has conducted over 1,000 AI calls during its pilot phase and helped close a few roles, Rathi said\.

He did not disclose the number of unique users who participated or the number of jobs filled\.Profound opened its waitlist on August 4\. Users can try an introductory voice interaction, while broader representation and matching features will be released gradually to selected groups\.Rathi said the system has initially been tested across engineering, product, design, marketing, analyst and chief-of-staff roles\. The AI Rep will not independently contact people or pursue opportunities without the user’s approval\.“The Rep does not go and automatically do it\. It speaks with you about what it is going to write and what should be adjusted\. You are in control,” he said\.Hiring is expected to be among Profound’s first revenue streams\. The company may also explore professional subscriptions and, later, business introductions through its network\.The funding will be used to expand its product and engineering teams and strengthen its AI and matching capabilities\.

# Profound Raises $1\.5M Seed Funding From Swiggy, Zomato Founders

Former Swiggy and Zomato executives have raised $1\.5 million in seed funding for their new AI startup, Profound\. The company is developing an AI representative designed to help professionals find career opportunities and build networks\. The capital will be used to grow engineering and product teams ahead of a planned global rollout for one million users\.

Anuj Rathi, a former senior executive at Swiggy, and Prashant Parashar, formerly of Zomato, have officially launched their artificial intelligence venture, Profound\. The startup announced on Monday that it has secured $1\.5 million in a seed funding round\. The investment highlights continued interest from established tech entrepreneurs in AI-based solutions for the labor market\.

### AI-Powered Career Representation

Profound is building an AI-powered representative, or AI Rep, which aims to act as a personal agent for professionals\. The system is designed to learn a user's career history, skills, and future goals through voice-based interactions\. By capturing this context, the AI identifies potential career opportunities and facilitates professional connections\. The founders aim to replicate the agency model commonly used in sports and entertainment, but for general professional talent\.

### Backing From Tech Industry Leaders

The funding round attracted participation from several prominent figures in the Indian startup ecosystem\. Key investors include Swiggy co-founders Sriharsha Majety and Nandan Reddy, Zomato co-founder Pankaj Chaddah, and Razorpay CEO Harshil Mathur\. Other notable investors include Kunal Shah, an executive at WhatsApp, and Bhuvan Gupta, co-founder of OfBusiness\. Institutional backing was provided by Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital\.

### Product Development and Hiring Features

Profound plans to direct these funds toward expanding its engineering and product teams\. A primary goal is to enhance the AI's core capabilities, specifically its reasoning engine that translates voice conversations into actionable career insights\.

Beyond individual users, the startup is also developing features for hiring managers\. This service allows companies to create AI Reps for specific job roles to better match candidates based on context rather than relying solely on traditional, static resumes\. The company aims to onboard one million professionals globally over the next year\.

### Investor Perspective on Talent Discovery

Investors backing the startup have pointed to the persistent inefficiency in how talent is discovered and matched with opportunities\. By utilizing a voice-first, AI-native approach, the founders are attempting to address the limitations of keyword-based search systems currently used in professional networking\. The next phase for the company involves scaling its infrastructure and moving toward a broader beta rollout, which will provide further clarity on how effectively the tool can translate user context into successful professional introductions\.

# Former Swiggy and Zomato leaders launch Profound

Anuj Rathi and Prashant Parashar, former product and technology leaders with experience across Swiggy, Zomato, Cleartrip, Flipkart, Ola and Walmart Labs, today announced the launch of Profound, a global AI-native platform where every professional gets their own AI Rep\. The company has also raised a $1\.5 million seed round and opened early access to its first cohort following several months of product development and user research\. Together, Rathi and Parashar bring more than two decades of experience building global products, growth systems and technology platforms that have served millions of users\.

The seed round includes participation from technology founders and entrepreneurs, including **Sriharsha Majety, CEO, Swiggy; Nandan Reddy, Co-Founder, Swiggy; Pankaj Chaddah, ex-Zomato; Harshil Mathur, CEO, Razorpay; Kunal Shah, Global Head, WhatsApp; and Bhuvan Gupta, Co-Founder, OfBusiness,** among others\. The round also includes institutional participation from **Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital**\.

The company will use the funding to strengthen its engineering and product teams, expand its AI capabilities and accelerate development of its matching and introductions engine\. Over the next year, Profound plans to build its founding network and onboard 1 million professionals globally ahead of a broader beta rollout\.

Commenting on the launch, **Anuj Rathi, Co-Founder and CEO, Profound**, said, “Just as actors have agents and athletes have managers, Profound gives each professional their own AI Rep\. It learns your work and your judgment, and keeps you ready for the next move and the connection that has the potential to change your career trajectory\. This is what the future of work looks like when representation is available to everyone\.”

At Profound, every professional receives an AI Rep that begins with a 30-minute voice conversation\. It develops a continuously evolving understanding of a person’s experience, expertise, judgment, working style, ambitions and context\. The AI Rep works in the background on behalf of professionals, identifies relevant opportunities, facilitates meaningful introductions and helps build stronger professional relationships and careers\.

**Prashant Parashar, Co-Founder and CTO, Profound**, said, “Voice AI has reached a point where a machine can hold a genuinely curious conversation\. We built the reasoning layer that turns those conversations into an AI Rep\. That richer understanding of a professional enables significantly better matches, shifting professional discovery from keyword-based search to intelligence-driven matchmaking\.”

Profound also enables hiring managers to create AI Reps for roles and teams\. Through natural conversations, founders and hiring leaders can capture far deeper context than a conventional job description, enabling more accurate talent discovery, stronger matches, meaningful introductions and more effective collaboration\.

**Rahul Chowdhri, Partner at Stellaris Venture Partners**, said, “There’s a growing gap between how good someone is at their job and how easy they are to find\. Resumes and LinkedIn profiles capture titles, not judgment\. Profound uses a voice-first, AI-native approach to build an always-on ‘AI Rep’ that represents professionals with far greater depth\. We are excited to back the team as they build the professional OS for the AI era\.”

**Pranav Pai, Managing Partner at 3one4 Capital,** said, “The biggest constraint in hiring today is not the supply of talent but the ability to verify fit\. Resumes and static profiles cannot capture judgment, working style or real context\. Profound is rebuilding that layer for an AI-first world, and we are backing the team as they redefine how professionals are understood and matched\.”

Profound is now available through an early-access programme for its first cohort, with broader beta access planned later this year\. Looking ahead, the company envisions a professional ecosystem where AI Reps interact with one another on behalf of individuals and organisations, enabling richer discovery, trusted introductions, and new ways to build careers, teams, and businesses\. At its core, Profound is building toward a future where AI is not just representing people, but co-creating intelligent agency throughout their professional journey\.

# Profound Raises $1\.5M Seed Funding From Swiggy, Zomato Founders

Founded by former Swiggy and Zomato executives, the company aims to help professionals manage career opportunities through personalized AI representatives\. For organizations, the company intends to offer these AI tools to streamline talent acquisition and internal collaboration\.

### Backing from Tech Founders and Institutional Investors

The funding round attracted significant interest from key figures within the Indian technology and startup ecosystem\. Early-stage backers include Swiggy co-founders Sriharsha Majety and Nandan Reddy, along with early Zomato leader Pankaj Chaddah and Razorpay CEO Harshil Mathur\. These firms have previously backed various SaaS and consumer-tech ventures, and their involvement suggests a focus on the platform's potential to address inefficiencies in professional discoverability and hiring\.

### Operational Goals and Market Strategy

Profound has stated that the newly acquired funds will be directed toward building out its proprietary matching engine and enhancing its voice-AI technology\. The company's roadmap includes building a network of founding users with an ambitious target of onboarding one million professionals globally before its broader beta launch\.

From a business perspective, the company is positioning itself in the growing segment of AI-enabled professional services\. While the sector has seen a surge in interest due to advancements in large language models and voice AI, startups in this space often face challenges related to user adoption, the quality of AI-driven recommendations, and competition from established professional networking platforms like LinkedIn\.

Investors and observers should monitor how Profound manages the transition from product development to large-scale user acquisition\. Key factors for the company’s success will include its ability to prove the accuracy of its matching engine, data privacy management, and its ability to integrate with existing enterprise hiring workflows\. As the product moves toward a public beta, the company’s ability to maintain high engagement levels and demonstrate actual hiring or networking success for its users will be the primary metric for its growth\.

## Former Swiggy and Zomato Executives Launch AI Startup Profound with $1\.5 Million Seed Round

Two former executives from India’s leading food delivery platforms, Swiggy and Zomato, have launched an artificial intelligence startup called Profound, securing $1\.5 million in a seed funding round, according to a report by Entrackr\. The move marks a significant entry of industry veterans into the AI space, leveraging their experience in scaling tech-driven services\.

## Background of the Founders

The startup’s founders, whose names were not disclosed in the report, previously held leadership roles at Swiggy and Zomato, two of India’s most prominent food delivery companies\. Their expertise spans operations, product development, and data-driven decision-making—areas critical to building AI solutions for the food and logistics sectors\. While Entrackr did not name the individuals, industry insiders suggest the team includes former executives with a track record in optimizing supply chains and customer engagement\.

## Focus on AI-Driven Solutions

Profound aims to develop AI tools tailored for the restaurant and delivery industries, with an emphasis on predictive analytics, demand forecasting, and operational efficiency\. The startup’s initial focus is on helping small and medium-sized restaurants streamline inventory management and reduce food waste, according to the report\. This aligns with broader trends in AI adoption within the food tech sector, where companies are increasingly investing in machine learning to cut costs and improve service delivery\.

The $1\.5 million seed round was led by a group of angel investors, though specific names or firms were not disclosed\. Entrackr noted that the funding will be used to expand the startup’s engineering team and pilot its technology with select restaurant chains\. The round follows a surge in AI venture capital investments in India, where the sector attracted over $1\.2 billion in 2023, according to a Nasscom report\.

## Industry Reactions and Potential Impact

Industry analysts have greeted the launch with cautious optimism\. “The combination of deep domain knowledge from the food tech space and AI expertise could create a unique value proposition,” said a researcher at the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, who was not involved in the startup\. However, challenges remain, including competition from established AI firms and the need to demonstrate measurable ROI for restaurant operators\.

## What’s Next for Profound?

The startup plans to launch a minimum viable product by the end of 2024, with a focus on scalability and integration with existing restaurant management systems\. If successful, Profound could position itself as a key player in India’s growing AI ecosystem, particularly in sectors reliant on real-time data processing and optimization\.
